title: Back-rank mate
line: A rook or queen on the last rank, the king boxed in by its own pawns.

steps.text: The king on g8 is boxed in by its own pawns. A rook on the back rank, the king's first row, gives mate.
Black's queen is far away. Mate on the back rank.
steps.hint: The rook moves straight up to the back rank.
steps.after: Checkmate. The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 take every square from their own king.

steps.text: Here Black's two rooks guard the back rank. Against two white rooks on the same file, the first one takes and the second one mates.
Take the rook on e8, with check.
steps.after: The rook on a8 had to take back, and now it stands alone on e8.

steps.text: Now mate with the other rook.
Now you are Black, and the back rank is weak. Give your king a square first: move one of the pawns in front of it.

wrong.c8d8: Then the rook takes on d8, and it is checkmate.
wrong.c8c7: Then the rook goes to d8, and it is checkmate.

wrong.f7f5: That gives the king a square, but the pawn on f5 has no pawn beside it to guard it.

steps.hint: A pawn that steps forward leaves an empty square for the king.
steps.after: The king has a square. A check on the back rank is no longer mate.

summary: A king behind three unmoved pawns can be mated on its back rank. Give it a square in time.
